bill_ref: Workplace Legislation Amendment (Accident Compensation and Other Matters) Bill 2026
name: Workplace Legislation Amendment (Accident Compensation and Other Matters) Bill 2026
question: That the Workplace Legislation Amendment (Accident Compensation and Other Matters) Bill 2026 be divided into two Bills as follows: (a) A Workplace Legislation Amendment (Compensation and Other Matters) Bill 2026 being the Workplace Legislation Amendment (Accident Compensation and Other Matters) Bill 2026 with the following changes: (i) Long title as follows: “A Bill for an Act to amend the Workplace Injury Rehabilitation and Compensation Act 2013 in relation to guarantees and supported accommodation, the Accident Compensation Act 1985 in relation to supported accommodation, the Transport Accident Act 1986 in relation to supported accommodation, the Occupational Health and Safety Act 2004 in relation to coercive conduct and to make consequential amendments to the Occupational Health and Safety Amendment (Dangerous Goods) Act 2026 and for other purposes.”; (ii) Short title as follows: “Workplace Legislation Amendment (Compensation and Other Matters) Bill 2026”; (iii) Heading to Part 1; (iv) Clause 1 as follows: “1 Purposes The main purposes of this Act are – (a) to amend the Workplace Injury Rehabilitation and Compensation Act 2013 – (i) to make further provision for guarantees obtained for the purposes of that Act; and (ii) in relation to supported accommodation; and (b) to amend the Accident Compensation Act 1985 in relation to supported accommodation; and (c) to amend the Occupational Health and Safety Act 2004 to prohibit coercive conduct; and (d) to amend the Transport Accident Act 1986 in relation to supported accommodation; and (e) to make consequential amendments to the Occupational Health and Safety Amendment (Dangerous Goods) Act 2026; and (f) to make other miscellaneous and technical amendments to those Acts.”; (v) Clause 2; (vi) Heading to Part 2; (vii) Heading to Division 1 of Part 2; (viii) Clauses 3 to 9; (ix) Heading to Division 2 of Part 2; (x) Clause 10; (xi) Clause 11 as follows: ‘11 New section 630 inserted After section 629 of the Workplace Injury Rehabilitation and Compensation Act 2013insert – “630 Transitional provision – Workplace Legislation Amendment (Compensation and Other Matters) Act 2026 (1) The definition in section 223(1) of supported accommodation, as amended by Division 2 of Part 2 of the amending Act, applies and is taken to have always applied in respect of a liability for compensation payable under section 224 to a person who resides in supported accommodation on or after 1 July 2024. (2) In this section – amending Act means the Workplace Legislation Amendment (Compensation and Other Matters) Act 2026.”.’; (xii) Clauses 12 and 13; (xiii) Heading to Part 3; (xiv) Clause 14; (xv) Clause 15 as follows: ‘15 New Division 20 of Part IX inserted After Division 19 of Part IX of the Accident Compensation Act 1985insert – “Division 20 – Workplace Legislation Amendment (Compensation and Other Matters) Act 2026 401 Supported accommodation (1) The definition in section 99AAA(1) of supported accommodation, as amended by Part 3 of the amending Act, applies and is taken to have always applied in respect of a liability for compensation payable under section 99 to a person who resides in supported accommodation on or after 1 July 2024. (2) In this section – amending Act means the Workplace Legislation Amendment (Compensation and Other Matters) Act 2026.”.’; (xvi) Heading to Part 4; (xvii) Clauses 16 and 17; (xviii) Clause 18 as follows: ‘18 New Division 15 of Part 11 inserted After Division 14 of Part 11 of the Transport Accident Act 1986insert – “Division 15 – Workplace Legislation Amendment (Compensation and Other Matters) Act 2026 235 Supported accommodation (1) The definition of supported accommodation, as amended by Part 4 of the amending Act, applies and is taken to have always applied in respect of a liability for compensation payable under section 60 to a person who resides in supported accommodation on or after 1 July 2024. (2) In this section – amending Act means the Workplace Legislation Amendment (Compensation and Other Matters) Act 2026.”.’; (xix) Heading to Part 5; (xx) Heading to Division 1 of Part 5; (xxi) Clauses 19 and 20; (xxii) Clause 21 as follows: ‘21 Disqualification of health and safety representatives (1) For section 56(1)(d) of the Occupational Health and Safety Act 2004substitute – “(d) intentionally used, disclosed or provided to another person, for a purpose not reasonably connected with the exercise of a power under this Part – (i) photographs or measurements taken or sketches or recordings made in the exercise of a power under section 58(1)(ab); or (ii) any other information the health and safety representative acquired from an employer in the exercise of a power under this Part; (e) published or caused to be published, for a purpose not reasonably connected with the exercise of a power under this Part, any information referred to in paragraph (d); (f) published online or caused to be published online any information referred to in paragraph (d).”. (2) After section 56(3) of the Occupational Health and Safety Act 2004insert – “(4) In this section – publish has the same meaning as in section 91; publish online has the same meaning as in section 91.”.’; (xxiii) Clause 22 of the Bill omitted. (xxiv) Clause 23 renumbered 22 as follows: ‘22 New section 58A inserted After section 58 of the Occupational Health and Safety Act 2004insert – “58A Health and safety representative must not publish certain information online (1) A health and safety representative for a designated work group must not publish online or cause to be published online any of the following information – (a) photographs or measurements taken or sketches or recordings made in the exercise of a power under section 58(1)(ab); (b) any other information the health and safety representative acquired from an employer in the exercise of a power under this Part. Note See section 56(1)(f). (2) In this section – publish online has the same meaning as in section 91.”.’; (xxv) Clause 24 renumbered 23; (xxvi) Clause 25 of the Bill omitted; (xxvii) Clause 26 renumbered 24 as follows: ‘24 Section 88 amended For section 88(2) of the Occupational Health and Safety Act 2004substitute – “(2) A notice given under subsection (1) must – (a) be in writing in the form approved by the Authority; and (b) include a description of the suspected contravention.”.’; (xxviii) Clause 27 of the Bill omitted; (xxix) Clause 28 renumbered 25 as follows: ‘25 Offences by authorised representatives (1) For section 91(ca) of the Occupational Health and Safety Act 2004substitute – “(ca) intentionally use, disclose or provide to another person, for a purpose not reasonably connected with the exercise of a power under this Part, photographs or measurements taken or sketches or recordings made in the exercise of a power under section 89(1)(ba); or (cb) publish or cause to be published, for a purpose not reasonably connected with the exercise of a power under this Part, any information referred to in paragraph (c) or (ca); or (cc) publish online or cause to be published online any information referred to in paragraph (c) or (ca); or”. (2) At the end of section 91 of the Occupational Health and Safety Act 2004insert – “(2) In this section – publish means to disseminate or provide access to the public or a section of the public by any means, including by – (a) publication in a book, newspaper, magazine or other written publication; or (b) broadcast by radio or television or on the Internet; or (c) public exhibition; or (d) electronic communication (including social media); publishonline means to disseminate or provide access to the public or a section of the public by – (a) broadcast on the Internet; or (b) electronic communication (including social media).”.’; (xxx) Clauses 29 and 30 renumbered 26 and 27; (xxxi) Heading to Division 2 of Part 5; (xxxii) Clauses 31 to 33 renumbered 28 to 30; (xxxiii) Clause 34 renumbered 31 as follows: ‘31 New section 99A inserted After section 99 of the Occupational Health and Safety Amendment (Dangerous Goods) Act 2026 insert – ‘99A Health and safety representative must not publish information online In section 58A(1)(b) of the Principal Act, for “Part” substitute “Chapter”.’.’; (xxxiv) Clauses 35 to 37 renumbered 32 to 34; (xxxv) Heading to Part 6; (xxxvi) Clause 38 renumbered 35; (b) An Occupational Health and Safety Amendment (Representative Powers) Bill 2026 being the Workplace Legislation Amendment (Accident Compensation and Other Matters) Bill 2026 with the following changes: (i) Long title as follows: “A Bill for an Act to amend the Occupational Health and Safety Act 2004 in relation to the powers of representatives and to make consequential amendments to the Occupational Health and Safety Amendment (Dangerous Goods) Act 2026 and for other purposes.”; (ii) Short title as follows: “Occupational Health and Safety Amendment (Representative Powers) Bill 2026”; (iii) Heading to Part 1; (iv) Clause 1 as follows: “1 Purposes The main purposes of this Act are – (a) to amend the Occupational Health and Safety Act 2004 to make further provision for the powers of authorised representatives and health and safety representatives; and (b) to make consequential amendments to the Occupational Health and Safety Amendment (Dangerous Goods) Act 2026; and (c) to make other miscellaneous and technical amendments to those Acts.”; (v) Clause 2 as follows: “2 Commencement (1) Subject to subsection (2), the provisions of this Act come into operation on a day or days to be proclaimed. (2) If a provision of this Act does not come into operation before 10 September 2027, it comes into operation on that day.”; (vi) Heading to Part 2 of the Bill omitted; (vii) Heading to Division 1 of Part 2 of the Bill omitted; (viii) Clauses 3 to 9 of the Bill omitted; (ix) Heading to Division 2 of Part 2 of the Bill omitted; (x) Clauses 10 to 13 of the Bill omitted; (xi) Heading to Part 3 of the Bill omitted; (xii) Clauses 14 and 15 of the Bill omitted; (xiii) Heading to Part 4 of the Bill omitted; (xiv) Clauses 16 to 18 of the Bill omitted; (xv) Heading to Part 5 renumbered 2; (xvi) Heading to Division 1 of Part 5 of the Bill omitted; (xvii) Clauses 19 and 20 of the Bill omitted; (xviii) Clause 21 renumbered 3 as follows: ‘3 Disqualification of health and safety representatives (1) After section 56(1)(c) of the Occupational Health and Safety Act 2004insert – “(ca) intentionally used, disclosed or provided to another person, for a purpose not reasonably connected with the exercise of a power under this Part, copies or extracts of documents made or taken in the exercise of a power under section 58(1)(ac);”.’; (xix) Clause 22 renumbered 4; (xx) Clause 23 renumbered 5 as follows: ‘5 New section 58B inserted Before section 59 of the Occupational Health and Safety Act 2004insert – “58B Health and safety representative must not publish copies or extracts of documents online (1) A health and safety representative for a designated work group must not publish online or cause to be published online any copies or extracts of documents made or taken in the exercise of a power under section 58(1)(ac). (2) In this section – publish online means to disseminate or provide access to the public or a section of the public by – (a) broadcast on the Internet; or (b) electronic communication (including social media).”.’; (xxi) Clause 24 of the Bill omitted; (xxii) Clause 25 renumbered 6; (xxiii) Clause 26 renumbered 7 as follows: ‘7 Section 88 amended (1) For the heading to section 88 of the Occupational Health and Safety Act 2004 substitute – “Notice of entry and enquiry into suspected contravention”. (2) After section 88(2) of the Occupational Health and Safety Act 2004insert – “(3) An authorised representative who enters a place under section 87 and identifies another suspected contravention at the place must, before enquiring into the suspected contravention, take all reasonable steps to give notice of the suspected contravention in accordance with subsection (1).”.’; (xxxiv) Clause 27 renumbered 8; (xxxv) Clause 28 renumbered 9 as follows: ‘9 Offences by authorised representatives (1) After section 91(ca) of the Occupational Health and Safety Act 2004insert – “(cab) intentionally use, disclose or provide to another person, for a purpose not reasonably connected with the exercise of a power under this Part, copies or extracts of documents made or taken in the exercise of a power under section 89(1)(bb); or”. (2) In section 91(cb) and (cc) of the Occupational Health and Safety Act 2004, for “paragraph (c) or (ca)” substitute “paragraph (c), (ca) or (cab)”.’; (xxvi) Clauses 29 and 30 of the Bill omitted; (xxvii) Heading to Division 2 of Part 5 of the Bill omitted; (xxviii) Heading to Part 3 as follows: “Part 3 – Amendment of Occupational Health and Safety Amendment (Dangerous Goods) Act 2026”; (xxix) Clauses 31 and 32 omitted; (xxx) Clause 33 renumbered 10 as follows: ‘10 New section 97AA inserted After section 97 of the Occupational Health and Safety Amendment (Dangerous Goods) Act 2026 insert – ‘97AA Disqualification of health and safety representatives In section 56(1)(c) and (ca) of the Principal Act, for “Part” (wherever occurring) substitute “Chapter”.’.’; (xxxi) Clause 34 of the Bill omitted; (xxxii) Clause 35 renumbered 11 as follows: ‘11 Offences by authorised representatives In section 133 of the Occupational Health and Safety Amendment (Dangerous Goods) Act 2026, after “(ca)” insert “, (cab)”.’; (xxxiii) Clauses 36 and 37 of the Bill omitted; (xxiv) Heading to Part 6 renumbered 4; (xxv) Clause 38 renumbered 12.
